candidates.title: Prepare game-test CSV rows for review

demandEvidence.chore: Exporting mobile game test logs from notes into Sheets without missed or repeated file processing.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I have tried a Schedule Trigger plus Google Drive Watch Files and also a Webhook from a shortcut on the phone, but the workflow either doesn’t fire at all or fires twice on the same file.

ease.reason: The supplied n8n docs describe scheduled Drive event checks and CSV-to-row extraction; phone upload timing and deduplication still need operator testing.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small game QA teams may pay for cleaner session logs; this one post shows a chore, not buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic CSV review flow fits the documented extraction step; real formats, trigger behavior and duplicate keys remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: Documented Drive polling can trigger on matching events and CSV extraction yields rows; a person must validate keys and import output.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe measured fields, a notes-to-CSV-to-Sheets habit and missed or repeated triggers; recurrence beyond this user is unknown.

experimentPlan.output: A review-ready table from a supplied game-test CSV, with duplicate rows flagged before import.
inputs: Synthetic CSV with frame drops and notes
experimentPlan.trigger: A tester supplies an exported sample CSV for one session.
steps: Extract CSV rows into structured fields.
Check required measurement columns.
Compare rows using the operator-selected key.
Flag repeated or incomplete rows.
Have a tester verify and import the reviewed table.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Run a labeled fictional CSV containing known complete, incomplete, and repeated rows; confirm extracted values match and only expected duplicates are flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A tester chooses the deduplication key, reviews every flagged row, and imports approved data; phone triggers and live Google Sheets writes are outside this proposed test.
unverified: Phone upload timing and trigger behavior remain unresolved.
The right duplicate key and real CSV formats are not supplied.

candidates.reason: Concrete task with limited n8n implementation support; prior below-threshold decision is reassessed using current supplied references, but the unresolved live trigger and duplicate contract keep it below threshold.

candidates.title: Draft shipment delay notices from supplied rows

demandEvidence.chore: Preparing a dispatcher alert when supplied shipment rows show a delay.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A simple flow can notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed, copy an order update into a CRM, alert a buyer when inventory drops, or send a daily report to a team channel.

ease.reason: The retained example names a clear notification output, but no supplied building reference documents shipment intake or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small ecommerce operators may pay for faster delay notices; the post gives examples, not buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A fictional row-to-draft prototype is bounded, but event access, status rules and delivery are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A sample rule can flag rows repeatedly, while a person must verify delay status and send the notice; no automation capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The task span lists shipment delay notifications as an example, but does not show a specific operator case, frequency or implementation.

experimentPlan.output: A review queue of proposed delay notices from a supplied shipment CSV.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator uploads a sample shipment CSV for review.
steps: Read the supplied fictional rows.
Flag rows meeting the operator threshold.
Fill a draft notice with supplied shipment fields.
Hold rows with missing or conflicting values.
Ask a person to approve each draft.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For labeled fictional rows, verify only the expected delayed rows are flagged and every draft field matches its input row.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies the threshold and wording, reviews every notice, and sends it manually; no shipment system access or delivery is proposed.
unverified: The source gives an example, not a buyer-specific recurring case.
Shipment data access and event timing are unverified.
No supplied reference supports message delivery.

candidates.reason: The source gives an example chore but no implementation reference; the proposed CSV mock is assessable and remains below threshold.

feasibility.reason: A fictional row-checking prototype is small, while live Apify access, costs and Google account setup are unverified.

experimentPlan.output: A review sheet that checks supplied weekly keyword metric rows for missing values and duplicates.

Check that each row has volume, CPC and difficulty fields.
Flag missing values and repeated keywords.
Keep source values unchanged in the output.
Have a person review flags before using the sheet.

unverified: No supplied reference supports Apify execution or Google Sheets writes.
